source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Give insulin lispro only at bedtime regardless of when meals are actually consumed","B":"Give insulin lispro within about 15 minutes before a meal or immediately after eating","C":"Give insulin lispro 30 to 60 minutes before meals as routinely done with regular insulin","D":"Give insulin lispro one hour after each meal to prevent early postprandial hypoglycemia"}}
source_row.rationale: Rapid-acting insulins such as lispro have a rapid onset of action (generally within about 15 minutes), so they are typically administered shortly before eating (or as specifically labeled for that product), unlike regular insulin, which requires a longer lead time of about 30-60 minutes before meals.
source_row.source_detail: Prescribing information dosage/administration: rapid-acting insulin lispro is administered shortly before a meal or immediately after, product-specific labeling governs exact timing; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client is prescribed insulin lispro, a rapid-acting insulin, to be taken before meals, and mentions a habit of taking their old, slower-acting insulin an hour before eating and assumes this new one should be timed the same way. The nurse should teach the client to instead administer this insulin:
